title: After Graduation: Five Different Paths
paragraphs: Every spring, thousands of students at universities across Kazakhstan begin asking themselves the same question: what next? At WKU, the final semester always buzzes with conversation about future plans. Some students already know exactly what they are going to do. Others are still deciding. And some are deliberately keeping their options open, convinced that certainty is overrated.

Kamila Seitkali, who is studying Linguistics in her final year, has a clear vision. "I'm going to apply for a master's programme in Edinburgh," she says without hesitation. "I've already started preparing my application. The deadline is in January, and I need three letters of recommendation." She smiles. "I know it's ambitious, but I've been working towards this for two years. It's not a dream anymore — it's a plan."

Amir Bekzhanov's plans are more immediate. "I'm going to join a tech startup in Almaty the month after graduation," he says. "I've already been offered a position. It's a small company — fifteen people — and I'm going to be working on AI integration for their product." He leans back in his chair. "I thought about applying to a big corporation, but honestly, I'll learn more in a startup environment. More responsibility, more variety."

Rustam Seilov is the most relaxed of the group. He has no plan — and he seems comfortable with that. "I'm going to take a month off first," he says. "Travel somewhere. Probably Altai. Then I'll figure it out." He shrugs. "I know what I don't want: I don't want to rush into something just because everyone else is. I'll know the right thing when I see it." His friends exchange glances, but nobody argues.

Zhibek Akhmetova, meanwhile, has decided to stay at WKU for a year as a research assistant. "Professor Aidarov offered me a position in the language acquisition lab. I wasn't expecting it at all — he called me last week." She looks genuinely surprised, even now. "I'm going to help with a research project on bilingual education in Kazakhstan. It's going to be published, hopefully. That would be amazing."

The fifth student is a quieter figure — Daniyar Omarov, who rarely talks about his plans in public. He is going to return to his hometown of Aktobe immediately after graduation. "My family runs a small business," he says simply. "I'm going to help expand it. My degree in Economics is going to be useful — finally." He doesn't elaborate, but there's confidence in his voice. Not every story needs to be ambitious by someone else's standards.

What strikes a visitor listening to these five conversations is how different the futures are — not just geographically, but emotionally. Some plans are tightly organised; others are barely sketched in pencil. Some students are racing towards something; others are deliberately slowing down. What they share is the awareness that the next six months will define a decade.

Kamila puts it best, perhaps. "The plan doesn't have to be perfect," she says. "It just has to be yours. Something you chose, not something you fell into by accident. That's the difference between a life you made and a life that happened to you."

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: So, Rustam — what are you actually going to do? Everyone's asking.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Travel first. Then I'll figure it out. I told you.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: That's not a plan. That's a delay.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Or it's a different kind of plan. Not everything needs a spreadsheet.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I think it's brave, actually. I couldn't do it. I need to know what's next.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: And that's fine for you. We're just different.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I'll be honest — I'm a bit jealous. I'll be at my desk in Almaty in July.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: You chose that, Amir. You want it.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: True. I'm going to love it, I think. It's just — the uncertainty of Rustam's life looks very peaceful from here.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Come visit me in Altai. Bring a tent.
